_: Structural assertions per operation — 'did the work actually happen', as
distinct from 'did anything publish'. Written from the frozen instruction
text in methodology/operations.md, authored BEFORE inspecting any arm's
output so they cannot be tuned to a result.
Matched on TITLES, never paths: both arms legitimately choose different
paths for the same page, and the instructions specify titles. Asserting on
paths would score a naming preference as a failure. The site-name suffix
('... | Godzilla Docs') is stripped before comparison.
Deliberately conservative. Only what the instruction plainly requires is
asserted. Operations whose outcome is a matter of judgement — 'make it
unmistakable that v3 is current', 'add a prominent notice', 'add a table of
contents' — carry no assertion, because a check for them would encode this
author's taste as ground truth. Their absence is a stated limitation: an
operation with no assertion is still reported on the older, weaker evidence.
A 'no duplicate titles' rule was written and then REMOVED after it fired on
two legitimate outcomes: the raw arm leaving meta-refresh redirect stubs at
vacated paths (a sound technique when links are literal paths, and one whose
clutter M6 already counts), and operation C1 deliberately publishing a v3
page alongside the v2 it supersedes. It was encoding a hunch as ground truth.
